policy_reference: Core Locations Maintenance Policy and Process, V-1.4, Y2026
check_point: Project Delivery Guidelines (MOP approval, PAC process)
observation: During the inspection, after assessing all swap activities conducted in the review period, total 4 sample activities were reported by region out of which one sample of DG Swap project executed in Gujranwala was analyzed in detail. It was observed that the Method of Procedure (MOP) document which was required to be approved by NOMC and Regional Facility prior to commencement of the swap activity was found not shared with NOMC HQ and no approval was also obtained in contrary to the requirement of the policy. Additionally, the reviewed MOP was issued and shared in January 2025 whereas the corresponding swap activity was executed in December 2025. The significant time gap between document issuance and activity execution and no evidence of CMPak approval of MOP in non compliance with the policy raises concerns regarding the continued validity and relevance of the MOP at the time of actual implementation. Furthermore, as mentioned in the policy, all project documents including Bill of Quantities (BOQ), PAT and PAC will be signed off by vendor & regional facilities lead & will finally be signed off by RCTO. However in this case, no PAC document was found as regional team informed that the approved PAT document is treated as an equivalent to the PAC. The policy document however, does not mention any documented guidance to establish the concept of approved PAT as a substitute for PAC. The absence of formally approved MOPs, undefined document validity requirements, and the non existence of a formal PAC process indicate weaknesses in project governance and non compliance with policy controls.
rectification_plan: MOPs for swap activities will be formally approved by NOMC HQ and Regional Facilities prior to activity commencement, with approval evidence retained; a validity/expiry requirement will be defined so MOPs are re-validated where a significant gap exists between issuance and execution. A formal PAC process will be established distinct from PAT, or the policy will be amended to explicitly recognize the approved PAT as PAC where intended. All project documents (BOQ, PAT, PAC) will be signed off by vendor, Regional Facilities Lead and RCTO as required.

policy_reference: Security Management Policy and Process, V-3.1, Y2024
check_point: Reporting of Theft/Damage/Burnt/Loss of Asset (ALERT portal compliance)
observation: A sample theft incident involving tower braces at Site 5996 (Ticket No. 20260324946), reported on 19 March 2026, was reviewed in detail. No formal documentary evidence is maintained recording the meetings conducted by CMPak RSOs with vendors to finalize any applicable penalties as required under the SOW/SLA. The regional team informed that such meetings are conducted physically therefore no such record is maintained. The Alert portal has a system limitation due to which regional team POCs were unable to provide evidence for closed tickets/cases, as closed tickets are not visible to them on the portal. The sample incident ticket was then verified from data available with HQ which showed that ticket was reported on 19th Mar and closed on 2nd Jun 2026. As per the approved policy, the MS Vendor RSO is required to close all tickets routed to CMPak RSO by the 1st of the subsequent month, along with the investigation report, remarks, and supporting evidence. However, the sample case remained open from 19 March 2026 until 02 June 2026, indicating non compliance with the prescribed timeline in the policy leading to delayed imposition of penalties further increasing chances of missed penalties. The absence of documented evidence for penalty finalization meetings, non adherence to ticket closure timelines, and limited visibility of closed tickets at the regional level increase the risk of inconsistent process execution, delayed resolution of security incidents, weak accountability, and ineffective monitoring of vendor performance. Furthermore, the policy is highly recommended to be reviewed and updated to accurately reflect the actual operational process.
rectification_plan: Penalty-finalization discussions with the MS vendor will be formally documented and retained (minutes/records) rather than concluded verbally. Ticket-closure timelines (closure by 1st of subsequent month) will be actively monitored, and coordination initiated with ALERT portal system owners to enable regional visibility of closed tickets/cases. The policy will be reviewed and updated to reflect the actual operational process.

policy_reference: Network Operations Management under MS Model
check_point: Provision of parts/consumables (5% minimum healthy spare stock)
observation: Review of spare parts and consumables management identified that no documented monthly record was maintained by the regional team to demonstrate compliance with the policy benchmark of 5% minimum healthy spare stock. The regional team was unable to demonstrate how the 5% threshold is calculated, monitored, or maintained across during the audit periods. Hence policy compliance can not be assured. While monthly audits of spare parts are being conducted based on preventive maintenance requirements, however, absence of a formal documentation and tracking mechanism indicating the 5% minimum stock benchmark reflects that the policy requirement is not being applied or validated. Furthermore, no benchmark was available to determine the adequacy of spare parts and consumables required for corrective maintenance activities, limiting the ability to assess whether sufficient stock levels are maintained to support fault rectification requirements. This reflects non-compliance with policy requirements and indicates weak controls over spare parts stock management.
rectification_plan: A formal monthly stock monitoring and reporting mechanism will be implemented to document the 5% minimum healthy spare stock benchmark, the underlying calculation methodology, and the compliance status for each period. A benchmark for corrective-maintenance spares adequacy will also be defined. Supporting UAC records and spare-stock calculations will be retained monthly to evidence compliance.

policy_reference: NOMC Inventory Management & Spares Ordering Policy
check_point: Warehousing of Assets with MS Vendor (Quarterly audits)
observation: 1. During the review process it has been observed that the Quarterly frequency of MS Vendor Warehouse Audit for availability/utilization of spares is not being followed. Furthermore, the audit evidences shared indicates that audit is being conducted only for non-Telco Parts whereas the policy does not segregate the requirement of audit between telco and non-telco parts. Therefore Quarterly audit of MS Vendor warehouse for availability and utilization of spare parts is not compliant to the policy. 2. Secondly it has also been observed that quarterly general audit of MS Vendor Warehouse is not being conducted and neither audit reporting is being submitted to NOMC POC in HQ. Since there are no regular quarterly MS Vendor Warehouse audits for telco parts, no general audit conducted, no warehouse audit reports are generated and submitted to NOMC HQ, it results in ineffective inventory control, undetected discrepancies in spare parts stock, and inadequate oversight of warehouse operations. The exclusion of Telco parts from the audit scope further increases the risk of unreported shortages, misuse or mismanagement of critical inventory. Consequently, this may lead to operational inefficiencies, service disruptions, financial losses, and non-compliance with established policies and procedures.
rectification_plan: Quarterly audits of MS vendor warehouses will be conducted at the required frequency, covering both Telco and non-Telco parts (no segregation), for availability/utilization of spares. The separate quarterly general warehouse audit will be conducted per the defined template and the audit reports submitted to the NOMC POC at HQ. A Telco base spares list will be obtained/locked to enable Telco-part audit coverage.

policy_reference: Network Operations Management under MS Model
check_point: Preventive Maintenance audits (10% sample)
observation: During the review, it was observed that there is no centralized mechanism for retention and retrieval of preventive maintenance audit records. As a result, audit forms for a number of preventive maintenance audits were not available, limiting the ability to independently verify compliance with the mentioned policy requirements. Further review of preventive maintenance audits for C5 Sub-Region for March 2026 revealed that the MS Vendor performed 477 preventive maintenance activities during the month. Accordingly, 48 audits were required to be conducted by the regional team to meet the policy requirement of auditing 10% of the completed preventive maintenance activities. However, only 35 audit forms were provided as evidence, which is lower than the required 10% count as per policy. In addition, review of the available 35 audit forms identified inconsistencies in audit documentation: As per provided PM report for Mar 26, PM of site 4091 was performed on Mar 9, 2026, whereas date mentioned on PM audit form is Mar 5, 2026 which is prior to PM performed date. Evidence has been submitted for PM Audit performed for site 4203, however, site 4203 is not part of Preventive Maintenance Report for Mar 2026. Inconsistencies of similar nature have been identified for rest of the submitted evidences as well. Similar observation has also been highlighted in the Outsourcing Management of Support & Services Special Audit, where a lower than required number of PM audit samples was previously identified as well. This indicates inadequate compliance with the defined control mentioned in the policy, as the absence of a centralized mechanism for retention and tracking of audit forms has resulted in missing audit forms and limited ability to independently verify adherence to the prescribed 10% sampling requirement.
rectification_plan: A centralized mechanism for retention, retrieval and tracking of PM audit records will be implemented to ensure the 10% sampling requirement is evidenced per sub-region/grid. The EOMS audit mechanism will be enhanced and the policy amended so that system-based (soft) audits are formally recognized as valid PM audit evidence. Documentation inconsistencies identified (e.g. site 4091 date mismatch, site 4203 not in the PM report) will be corrected and controls added to prevent recurrence.

policy_reference: Network Operations Management under MS Model
check_point: Pro-rata compensation for newly on-air sites
observation: Review of monthly BOQs and vendor payments identified that newly operational sites are being compensated on a full-month basis without applying the required pro-rata adjustment. During the audit period, in central region, a total of 494 sites became operational at various points during the year. Testing of a sample of 30 newly on-air sites (on aired during mid of the month) revealed that the MS vendor was compensated for these sites on a full month basis for the respective on-air month, instead of applying pro-rata charges from the actual on-air dates. As a result, the vendor was paid PKR 344,105 against these sites, whereas payable amount calculated on a pro-rata basis was PKR 207,014, resulting in an excess payment of PKR 137,091. Additionally, BOQs were approved and vendor payments were processed contrary to policy requirements, leading to vendor over payments and inaccurate maintenance service costs. Furthermore, as the analysis was conducted on sample basis due to scope and time limitation, it is recommended that a detailed review of the remaining sites should also be conducted to verify whether vendor was compensated on full payment basis for remaining on air sites during their on air month as well.
rectification_plan: Pro-rata compensation for newly on-air sites will be applied from the actual on-air date in the monthly BOQ/UAC. The current practice and contractual arrangement will be reviewed with stakeholders and clarified in future MS contracts/RFPs to remove ambiguity between operational practice and policy. The identified excess payment of PKR 137,091 against the 30 sampled sites will be reconciled and adjusted, and a detailed review of the remaining sites (of 494) will be conducted to identify and recover any further over-payments.

policy_reference: Core Locations Maintenance Policy and Process, V-1.4, Y2026
check_point: Corrective Maintenance (SLA compliance, PO issuance, penalty enforcement)
observation: During the inspection, Corrective Maintenance (CM) cases from the review period were assessed. Based on criticality and recurrence, one sample relating to repeated "Low Suction Pressure Alarm at APC # 5" at KLP MSC Lahore was selected for detailed review. The alarm was found reported multiple times between 13 to 19 Jan 2026 and was escalated to the maintenance vendor, CNS Engineering, on each occurrence. Following several troubleshooting attempts, replacement of the expansion valve was identified as the required corrective action. However, despite the issue being classified as critical, the replacement was completed on 13 March 2026, resulting in a delay of approximately 53 days from the initial reporting of the issue. As per the contractual Service Level Agreement (SLA) with CNS Engineering, critical faults are required to be resolved within 24 hours. The observed resolution timeline significantly exceeded the prescribed SLA requirement. Furthermore, contractual provisions require penalties to be imposed for SLA breaches, however, no evidence was provided to demonstrate that any penalty had been applied for the delay. The regional team explained that the delay was associated with the process for part replacement, which required Purchase Order (PO) issuance by CMPak to the vendor prior to part replacement, however, the vendor was requested to engage prior to PO issuance to maintain network availability. As a result, regional team considers the vendor not contractually bound by the SLA during this period as PO was not issued to the vendor yet the vendor replaced the required part on best effort basis. A detailed review of the selected case and related transactions with CNS Engineering was further conducted. As per the contractual agreement between CMPak and CNS Engineering, no work execution is permitted without the issuance of a valid Purchase Order (PO). The contract further stipulates that, in cases where work is performed without a PO, the vendor shall be solely responsible for all associated costs and liabilities. Secondly, payments to the vendor will be made quarterly in arrears. However, it was observed that the vendor was specifically requested by CMPak to commence work prior to PO issuance in noncompliance to the contractual terms. This practice deviates from the contractual requirement and creates ambiguity regarding the applicability of contractual obligations, including Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance and penalty enforcement. Furthermore, analysis of payments and POs issued to the vendor revealed that no payments related to the current contract had been made to CNS Engineering during the review period of approximately 1.5 years. Historically, the payments to CNS Engineering have been found to be processed with a delay of approximately 1 to 1.5 years from the service provision which makes the validation of payments and their applicable penalties unverifiable. The prolonged delay in invoice processing and settlement increases the risk that applicable SLA penalties may not be timely assessed, deducted, or enforced. Additionally, no evidence was found to demonstrate that advance POs or alternative arrangements, which are recommended in such circumstances to facilitate urgent work while maintaining contractual compliance, had been issued. The execution of work prior to PO issuance, combined with the absence of clear guidelines governing SLA applicability during out of PO engagements and prolonged delays in vendor payment processing, creates ambiguity in contractual enforcement and results in inconsistent treatment of service delays, weak vendor accountability, and potential loss of recoverable penalties. Moreover, delayed resolution and settlement of such cases may adversely impact network reliability and operational effectiveness.
rectification_plan: A mechanism will be established to ensure a valid Purchase Order is issued to CNS Engineering before work commences, eliminating out-of-PO engagements and the resulting ambiguity over SLA/penalty applicability. The owner department will ensure timely vendor invoicing and FSR issuance so that quarterly payments and any SLA penalties are assessed and enforced without prolonged delay. The specific KLP MSC Lahore case (53-day delay) will be reviewed to determine penalty applicability, and guidelines governing SLA applicability and advance-PO arrangements for urgent works will be defined.

policy_reference: NOMC Electricity High Bill Reconciliation Policy and Process, V-2.3, Y2024
check_point: E-Tax/F-Tax reconciliation and exemption process
observation: During the assessment, it was observed that the policy prescribed process was not being complied. The regional team was found operating on an alternate process. Out of all DISCOs in the Central Region, sites pertaining to LESCO were selected for sample analysis. As per the practice adopted by the region, an exemption request letter was submitted to LESCO in January 2023 by regional team seeking waiver of E-Tax and F-Tax charges on CMPak sites. Any billing anomalies identified thereafter are communicated to LESCO through calls or WhatsApp for resolution. However, a review of LESCO invoices for January, April, and May 2026 revealed that multiple sites (44090, 44585, 44626, 44126, 44402, 43561P, and 44108) continued to be charged E-Tax and F-Tax despite the exemption request previously submitted to LESCO. As a sample, a detailed review of Site 44108 was conducted, the review identified instances where E and F Tax charges were paid by CMPak as follows: January 2026: PKR 29,028 (E-Tax) and PKR 6,831 (F-Tax), April 2026: PKR 57,956 (E-Tax) and PKR 13,636 (F-Tax), May 2026: PKR 64,385 (E-Tax) and PKR 15,149 (F-Tax). Similar charges were also observed in rest of the mentioned sites as well. Discussions with the regional team revealed that such cases are primarily followed up through informal communication channels, including telephone calls and WhatsApp messages, rather than through the formal reporting, application submission, and tracking mechanism prescribed in the policy. It was further noted that DISCOs typically require two to three months to resolve such matters, however, during this period CMPak continues to bear the tax charges, and no evidence was provided to demonstrate that these amounts are subsequently adjusted or recovered later once issue is resolved. Non compliance with the prescribed reconciliation and exemption process may result in continued payment of avoidable E-Tax and F-Tax charges, leading to unnecessary financial losses. Additionally, the lack of formal tracking and recovery mechanisms increases the risk of excess payments remaining unrecovered. Furthermore, a comprehensive review should be conducted across all DISCOs to identify sites where E-Tax/F-Tax exemptions have not been implemented despite prior notifications and are still being paid by CMPak, and to ensure timely recovery or adjustment of excess charges. The inconsistency between policy prescribed process and actual on-ground practice also highlights gaps where documented processes do not reflect the actual practices and require immediate alignment.
rectification_plan: The prescribed E-Tax/F-Tax reconciliation process (monthly reporting to Cost Control, Finance/FBR IRIS verification, formal DISCO exemption applications with receiving, and billing-cycle monitoring) will be adopted in place of the informal call/WhatsApp practice. Formal recovery applications for E-Tax/F-Tax already paid will be submitted per the SOP, documented, tracked and validated by Finance. A comprehensive review across all DISCOs will identify sites still being charged despite prior notifications, and paid amounts (including the identified LESCO sites) will be pursued for recovery/adjustment.

policy_reference: DG Maintenance & Management Policy and Process
check_point: DG Corrective Maintenance (Picture evidence archiving)
observation: A sample of six trouble tickets was selected for end-to-end verification of the process. The evidence provided against the sampled tickets, including TT snapshots, closure status, and rectification details, was reviewed and verified. During the review, it was observed that the picture evidence attached to the sampled tickets had been shared through WhatsApp. This practice was also confirmed by the regional POC, who stated that the pictures are typically presented when the vendor submits documentation for payment clearance (within 90 days). The policy does not specify WhatsApp as an approved channel for submission or archiving of the evidence. The process being implemented operationally is not formally defined within the policy. Due to the lack of proper archiving and documentation practices, there is a significant risk of data loss. Since pictorial evidence is currently being shared through WhatsApp, any records may become inaccessible if an employee resigns or leaves the organization. Furthermore, WhatsApp is not an official platform for data sharing. The prescribed procedure clearly states that all such information should be submitted through the designated online portal or mobile application which ensures audit traceability fir future references.
rectification_plan: Pictorial evidence of major parts replaced during DG corrective maintenance will be submitted and archived through the approved MS vendor application/online portal instead of WhatsApp, ensuring audit traceability. NOMC will be requested to establish a portal for snap-sharing and portal-based approval so that evidence is centrally retained and not lost on staff turnover.
